# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop through cells with black/white circle constraints on turning/straight behavior
- **Slitherlink** – Loop on grid edges/dots with numeric constraints on surrounding line segments
- **Mid-loop** – Loop through cells where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directed loop with wind constraints affecting movement
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop through rooms alternating between moon and sun symbols
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through cells with per-region constraints on circle behavior (all straight or all turning)
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in specified order

#### A2. Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop plus placement of black cells, with arrow/number clues indicating black cell counts in directions

### B. Path/Connection Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws paths connecting specific points (not necessarily forming a loop).

- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island nodes with 1–2 bridges; all islands connected; bridges don't cross
- **Pencils** – Mark out pencil shapes and draw lines from tips through a specified number of cells

### C. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver determines which cells to shade black (or leave white).

#### C1. Shading with Numeric Clues (Clue cells remain unshaded)
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers define white island sizes; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers indicate total visible white cells in four directions; black cells don't touch; whites connected
- **Kurotto** – Circled numbers indicate sum of adjacent contiguous black groups; circle cells stay white
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; all whites illuminated; no bulb-to-bulb visibility
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles in cells; numbers indicate adjacent triangle count; remaining white areas must form rectangles

#### C2. Shading with Regional Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Rooms with numbers dictating shaded cell count; whites can't span 3+ rooms in a line; shaded cells don't touch; whites connected
- **Norinori** – Each bold-lined region contains exactly two shaded cells; shaded cells form dominoes (pairs)
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white "promontories" (one white neighbor); numbers indicate white line length; no 2×2 of either color
- **Nurimeizu** – Rooms fully shaded or white; create maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not; no 2×2 of either color
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded connected; blocks in same region don't touch; no 2×2 shaded
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes don't touch (except corners); all shaded connected; no 2×2 shaded
- **Sto-stone** – Numbers indicate contiguous black cells per room; black cells don't connect across rooms; when "dropped" they fill bottom half
- **Usowan** – Numbers indicate adjacent shaded cells but one number per room is wrong; shaded cells don't touch; whites connected
- **Tilepaint** – Tiles (regions) are entirely shaded or unshaded; diagonal-cell numbers constrain black cell counts in rows/columns

#### C3. Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must form rectangles/squares; white groups must NOT form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size

#### C4. Shading by Elimination (given numbers, shade duplicates)
- **Hitori** – Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; shaded cells don't touch; whites connected

### D. Region Division / Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### D1. Partition into Specified Shapes
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes (5-cell blocks); numbers indicate surrounding block-boundary lines
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks (one cell wide); circles mark bends; arrows mark ends pointing to bends; numbers indicate block size

#### D2. Partition with Matching/Symmetry Constraints
- **Double Choco** – Divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape; numbers indicate half-block size

### E. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### E1. Latin-Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box

#### E2. Regional Number Fill
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbers; groups of same number form blocks of that size; same-sized blocks can't touch
- **Ripple Effect** – Rooms contain 1 to N; repeated numbers in a row/column must be spaced apart by at least the number's value
- **Makaro** – Rooms contain 1 to N; arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Nansuke** – Fill blank cells with digits from a given number list; numbers read left-to-right or top-to-bottom

#### E3. Symbol/Mark Placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference in counts; runs limited (— max 2 vertical, | max 2 horizontal)

### F. Object Placement / Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves objects within the grid.

#### F1. Placement
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes can't touch; line-of-sight attack constraints from head direction
- **Evolomino** – Place squares to form blocks on arrows; blocks along each arrow grow by one cell progressively

#### F2. Movement
- **Satogaeri** – Move circles within countries so each country has one; numbers indicate distance moved; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move all circles into gray areas via straight arrows; arrows don't cross or pass through other circles; gray area numbers equal sum of entering circles

### G. Block/Chain Construction
Puzzles where the solver determines which cells form blocks with specific connectivity and labeling rules.

- **Chained Block** – Determine black cells forming blocks; numbers indicate block size; blocks must chain (touch at corners); no duplicate size/shape within a chain

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Connectivity Constraints
*All white/unshaded cells must be connected:* Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Nurimeizu
*All shaded cells must be connected:* LITS, Nuritwin, Nurikabe (black wall)
*Single connected loop:* Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Yajilin
*All islands connected via bridges:* Hashiwokakero

### No 2×2 Constraints
*No 2×2 shaded:* Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin, Nurimisaki
*No 2×2 of either color:* Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki
*No 2×2 shaded or white:* Sto-stone (implied by checkerboard drop)

### Adjacency/Touching Prohibitions
*Shaded cells don't touch orthogonally:* Hitori, Heyawake, Usowan, Yajilin
*Same-type blocks don't touch:* Fillomino (same-sized), LITS (same-shaped tetrominoes)
*Snakes don't touch:* Hebi

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight
- Akari (light bulb illumination)
- Kurodoko (white cell counting in four directions)
- Hebi (snake attack line of sight)

### Directional/Arrow Clues
- Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Sashigane, Nagareru, Pencils, Yosenabe

---

## III. By Grid Element Type

### Dot/Edge-Based
- **Slitherlink** – Lines drawn on edges between dots
- **Hashiwokakero** – Bridges drawn between nodes

### Cell-Center-Based (Loop)
- Masyu, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Yajilin, Numberlink

### Cell-Based (Shading)
- Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Heyawake, Norinori, LITS, Hitori, Choco Banana, Shakashaka, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Akari, Chained Block

### Cell-Based (Number/Symbol Fill)
- Sudoku, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Juosan

### Cell-Based (Partitioning)
- Shikaku, Five Cells, Double Choco, Sashigane

### Cell-Based (Object Placement/Movement)
- Hebi, Evolomino, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Pencils
